name: CR1220

dimensions.note: Panasonic publishes maximum dimensions only; nominal is set to the maximum.

capacity_mah.conditions: Panasonic nominal capacity at 0.1 mA continuous standard drain; cutoff voltage not stated

variants.notes: Varta lists 35 mAh; GP lists 42 mAh. GP states a 10 year shelf life at room temperature.

variants.label: BR1220

capacity_mah.conditions: Panasonic nominal capacity at 0.03 mA continuous standard drain; cutoff not stated

variants.notes: BR1220 is a lithium-carbon-monofluoride battery in the same case. It has a flatter discharge curve and lower pulse capability than the CR type, and lower rated drain.

variants.label: VL1220

capacity_mah.conditions: Panasonic nominal capacity at 0.02 mA standard drain to 2.5 V, 20 °C

variants.notes: VL1220 is a rechargeable battery in the same case. About 1,000 charge-discharge cycles at 10% discharge depth, constant-voltage charging only. Not a drop-in replacement for the single-use CR battery unless the device is designed for it.

interchange.note: Same width and 0.4 mm thinner; lower capacity and may make poor contact in a CR1220 holder.
Same width and 0.5 mm thicker; fits only where the holder has the clearance.

notes: Wikipedia also lists an ML1220 manganese rechargeable battery in this size. Panasonic's VL1220 uses constant-voltage charging at 3.25 to 3.55 V.

safety: Swallowed coin batteries can cause severe internal burns within two hours. Keep batteries away from children, and seek emergency medical care immediately if one is swallowed or placed in the nose or ears.
In the United States, the National Battery Ingestion Hotline is 1-800-498-8666 and Poison Help is 1-800-222-1222.
Do not recharge, crush, puncture, heat or short-circuit a single-use lithium coin battery.
